title: Accra Life clothing and footwear catalogue
purpose: Production design brief for a broad, mix-and-match Ghanaian fashion wardrobe for player characters and NPCs.
important: This is a wardrobe specification, not a claim that every listed garment or shoe is already modelled or selectable in-game. Each asset must be created or sourced with suitable rights, fitted to both character rigs where appropriate, and tested before being presented as available.

principles.genderAvailability: Clothing and footwear are not hard-locked by gender. Any character can choose any compatible item.
principles.localIdentity: Represent Ghanaian everyday fashion and traditional clothing respectfully, including Fugu/Batakari, smocks, Kente, Ankara and locally familiar styling.
principles.mixAndMatch: Separate tops, bottoms, dresses, outerwear, footwear and accessories so players can combine items freely.
principles.colour: Support multiple colourways and patterns for each suitable item. Include solid colours, two-tone combinations, Ghana flag-inspired palettes, earth tones, bright colours, neutral colours and varied fabric patterns.
principles.realism: Use proper fitted 3D clothing meshes with fabric texture, seams, folds and believable silhouettes. Avoid the old cartoon primitive body/clothing look as the final target.
principles.npcVariation: NPC clothing should be selected with stable per-NPC outfit seeds, with varied colours and combinations across districts and occupations.
principles.performance: Reuse meshes/materials where possible, use texture atlases and LODs, and keep crowd clothing performant on phones.
principles.culture: Use appropriate local garment references and avoid treating every Ghanaian character as wearing the same ceremonial outfit.

categories.title: Ghanaian traditional and local wear
items: Fugu / Batakari smocks in short, regular and long lengths
Northern Ghanaian smock sets with matching trousers
Kente cloth outfits and Kente-accented shirts
Ankara / African print shirts and blouses
African print trousers and matching sets
Locally styled tunics and embroidered tops

categories.title: Footwear
items: Sneakers: low-top, high-top, running and chunky styles

patterns: Adinkra-inspired motifs used with cultural care
colourSystem.customisation: Where the garment design supports it, let the player select colourways or patterns independently for compatible clothing pieces. Footwear should support different upper, sole, lace and accent colours where practical.

npcWardrobeRules.districts: Vary looks naturally across Osu, Makola, East Legon, Airport City, Labadi, central Accra, estates, highway towns and Kumasi.
npcWardrobeRules.occupations: Use suitable uniform sets for police, security, health workers, market traders, drivers, bus attendants, mechanics, cleaners, hospitality staff and office workers.
npcWardrobeRules.uniforms: Role uniforms have required core pieces, but allow appropriate variation in fit, footwear and approved accessories. Do not dress police or medical staff in random civilian outfits while on duty.
npcWardrobeRules.consistency: Keep each NPC's outfit and colour choices stable between sessions where NPC persistence is supported.
npcWardrobeRules.diversity: Avoid obvious copy-paste crowds; vary garment combinations, colours, footwear, hairstyles and accessories.

playerSystems.wardrobe: Add a wardrobe interface with separate slots for top, bottom, outerwear, footwear and accessories.
playerSystems.shops: Support clothing and footwear shops, market stalls and boutiques in the game world.
playerSystems.barberAndStyle: Clothing selection should work alongside the hairstyle and barber systems.
playerSystems.saving: Persist item IDs, colour choices, patterns and equipped slots in the player appearance save.
playerSystems.economy: Items can have prices and shop availability later; do not block basic starter clothing behind premium purchases.

implementationStages: Create a small but high-quality representative set of local wear, streetwear, trousers, sneakers, clogs and slippers for both character rigs.
Build modular clothing attachment and fit validation for idle, walk, run and seated poses.
Add colour and pattern variants using reusable materials and texture atlases.
Create player wardrobe and save/load appearance data.
Add varied, role-appropriate NPC outfit pools with stable per-NPC selections.
Expand the catalogue in batches and test crowd performance on iPhone and ordinary computers.
